title: At the Restaurant
summary: A customer orders a meal, asks for the bill, and pays with a credit card.
description: A classic restaurant scenario for elementary learners. Vocabulary covers menu items, polite requests, paying methods, and tipping etiquette.

vocabulary.definition: the list of food and drinks available in a restaurant
the largest part of a meal, usually meat or fish with vegetables
the printed list of what you have to pay in a restaurant
a small plastic card used to pay for things

dialogue.text: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
Yes, a table for two, under the name Smith.
Perfect. Here is your menu. Can I get you something to drink?
Yes. A glass of red wine for me, and a still water, please.
I would like the grilled salmon with vegetables.
Excellent choice. I will be right back with your drinks.
Excuse me, can I have the bill, please?
Of course. Would you like to pay by cash or card?

questions.q: How many people are at the table?
What does the customer order to drink?
options: A glass of wine and still water

trueFalse.statement: The customer has a reservation under the name Smith.
trueFalse.explanation: Speaker 2 says 'a table for two, under the name Smith.'

teacherTips: Pre-teach the difference between 'still water' and 'sparkling water' — a frequent confusion in real restaurants abroad.
Use this dialogue as a model for polite requests: 'Can I have…?', 'I would like…'
After listening, students design a one-page menu and role-play ordering from it.

es.title: En el restaurante
es.summary: Un cliente pide una comida, pregunta por la cuenta y paga con tarjeta de crédito.
es.description: Un escenario clásico de restaurante para estudiantes de nivel elemental. El vocabulario cubre platos del menú, peticiones corteses, formas de pago y etiqueta de propina.

vocabulary.definition: la lista de comidas y bebidas disponibles en un restaurante
la parte principal de una comida, normalmente carne o pescado con verduras
la lista impresa de lo que tienes que pagar en un restaurante
una tarjeta de plástico pequeña que se usa para pagar

options: Una copa de vino y agua sin gas

trueFalse.statement: El cliente pide pollo a la parrilla.
trueFalse.explanation: El cliente pide salmón a la parrilla.

trueFalse.statement: El cliente tiene una reserva a nombre de Smith.
trueFalse.explanation: El interlocutor 2 dice 'a table for two, under the name Smith'.

teacherTips: Enseña antes la diferencia entre 'still water' y 'sparkling water', una confusión frecuente en restaurantes reales en el extranjero.
Usa este diálogo como modelo de peticiones corteses: 'Can I have…?', 'I would like…'.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes diseñan una página de menú y hacen el role-play pidiendo desde ella.
